header: The page image as I send it to the second reader (step 39f). A rendered page is a 300 dpi PNG of 2 to 3 MB (3.3 MB once encoded for sending) and the reader answers with a few hundred words. Measured on 19 Oct 2026 on one page (probe, same request twice): as stored, 2,506,817 bytes; as a JPEG with a long side of 2400 px at quality 85, 272,588 bytes (9 times fewer), the same 637 characters and the same 8 important numbers. The service shrinks large images itself (the page cost 1,359 input tokens either way), so the extra bytes buy nothing, and every byte is exposure to a slow or stalling connection. This never fails: any image that cannot be shrunk (or would not get smaller) is sent as it is.

symbols.name: shrinkForReading
symbols.sig: export async function shrinkForReading(image: Buffer, o: ShrinkOptions = {}): Promise<Buffer>
doc: Returns the page as a JPEG whose longest side is at most `edge` pixels; transparency becomes white. If that fails or the result is not smaller, I return the original.

behaviours: the defaults are the ones measured on the real page: 2400 px, quality 85
a heavy page becomes a JPEG
its long side is at most the given edge, and the shape is kept
it is far smaller than the PNG (at least 3 times here)
the default long side is 2400 px
a page already smaller than the edge is never enlarged
an image that would not get smaller is sent as it is
bytes that are not an image come back unchanged (never an error)
an empty buffer comes back unchanged
a fully transparent page becomes WHITE (not black)
